QUANTUM CLASSICALITY: NEW DEDUCTIONS AND SHARP BOUNDARIES
2026-10-07. Internal proof status; external correctness and priority unresolved.

Strongest actual deduction: a sharp receiver-growth phase diagram for the N61
copy-ladder obstruction. Let L,d>=2, m=2^(L-1),
H=direct_sum_{j=0}^{L-1} Sym^(2^j)(C^d), and
rho_psi=L^-1 direct_sum_j psi^(tensor 2^j). b_K is the best worst-state,
worst-receiver half-trace-distance error of one CPTP H->H^(tensor K), with
arbitrary correlated/entangled outputs and full input-algebra domain.

For every integer K>=1,

 b_K >= L^-1 sum_{2^j<K} [(d-1)/(d+2^j)](1-2^j/K),

 |b_K-min(log_2 K/L,1)| <= 1/L+(m+1)/(d+m).

Thus if d/m->infinity, uniformly in ANY receiver-count sequence K_L,

 b_(K_L)=min(log_2 K_L/L,1)+o(1),
 b_(K_L)->0 iff log K_L=o(L).

This is a necessary-and-sufficient growth threshold, beyond the supplied
N61 upper-only statement. The same finite exact (m+1)-design experiment
works for every K; a common faithful perturbation eta_L->0 loses at most
2eta_L in the lower bound and eta_L in the upper bound. e_EB->1 still holds.
There is no independent-clone or purification-preservation assertion.

Proof: the exact CPTP one-copy decoder sends every ladder member to psi.
For any proposed K broadcaster, restrict decoder-composed channel to each
input copy sector N=2^j. Haar/receiver-average universal cloning fidelity is
at most N/K+[(K-N)/K](N+1)/(N+d) for N<K, otherwise <=1. Sum over the uniform
input flag; geometric summation gives the lower bound. Binary splitting
gives upper ceil(log_2 K)/L, and a direct envelope gives the uniform formula.

Primary import: Keyl-Werner, Optimal Cloning of Pure States, Judging Single
Clones, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9807010 , Theorem 1 PDF p3, Section II
unrestricted-output convention p2, Section III.A symmetrization pp3-4.
The import permits arbitrary full tensor-product outputs; this is essential.
Full proof: ladder_many_receiver/PROOF.md.
Independent audit: ladder_many_receiver/cloning_simple/FULL_PROOF_AUDIT.md.

CURRENT RESEARCH STATE — 7 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane

DECISION
The strongest fully reconstructed result is the hard-energy discrimination law, selected for its self-contained proof, independent approaches, complete comparator and full-class finite-dimensional scope. The projected-Slater consequence has higher potential scientific reach but retains a new unimplemented counting-theorem dependency. Other consequential results are banked as research capital; they are not substitutes for further work on these leading mechanisms.

A. EXACT HARD-ENERGY DISCRIMINATION
Interface: known fixed finite H>=0 with unique zero ground, 0<E<=I and E|0>=|0>, parallel inputs, miss Tr(rho E^tensor n), exact support in Hsum<=Q. All separable inputs including mixtures and unequal products are the comparator. Input energy is charged; acquisition, idlers/adaptivity, nonzero false alarms, apparatus/control and preparation work are separate contracts.
Mechanism: energy-ordered upper Cholesky E=T* T, B=T^-1, A=B*B. Upper triangularity preserves cumulative energy cutoffs, so p_n(Q)=||B^tensor n P_Q||^-2 EXACTLY. This avoids exponentially damaging leakage in naive typical projection.
Full law: phi(s)=log||exp(-sH/2) A exp(-sH/2)||; g(c)=inf_s>=0[phi(s)+sc]. Uniformly in c>=0, n>=1, -log p_n(nc)=ng(c)-O(log(n+1)), with explicit fixed-(E,H,dimension) constants. The proof uses tensor-order converse and exact multinomial types of a tilted top eigenvector.
Free-use exponent: s*=inf{s:A<=exp(sH)}; -log p*(Q)=s*Q-O(logQ).
Separable law: levels h_j and ell_j=-log lambda_min(E restricted H<=h_j); exact finite allocation knapsack, asymptotic concave LP hull of (h_j,ell_j). eta=max ell_j/h_j. Advantage iff A is not <=exp(eta H).
Sharp structural principle: s*/eta <= number k of DISTINCT POSITIVE energy levels. Supremum k is approached by explicit weak rank-one effects with separated energies. Degeneracy does not increase this bound. At fixed nontrivial model equality for k>1 is not asserted.
Qutrit: H+=diag(1,2), E+=[[1/2,sqrt2/4],[sqrt2/4,3/4]]. s*=log((1+sqrt17)/2)=.9406136421072088, eta=log2, hard gain1.357018636860576; expected-energy exponent=(5/3)log2=1.155245300933242. Entanglement improves the fixed-use rate for EVERY0<c<2. Explicit Dicke probes have p<=C sqrt(Q+1) exp(-s*Q), an attainable second-order bound, not proved optimal second-order asymptotics.
Proofs: hard_energy_detection.
